messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — noticed a bunch of customer tickets asking why routing decisions sometimes look 'mystery-y'. Can we sketch a small explainer surface for route decisions?
Jon Reynolds: +1. Customers want deterministic reasons, not just 'fell back to cheaper model'.
Liya Chen: Important to balance explainability with performance and size of traces. We can't log the whole policy graph per request.
Sasha Ortiz: Quick thought: add an X-Route-Provenance header that contains a compact decision code + version. Then we can expand server-side for support. :bulb:
Maya Patel: That helps support, but product wants human-friendly strings too for webhooks/evals. Maybe header + optional expanded payload via /route-explain?id=...
Jon Reynolds: Agree. Implementation plan: compute a small decision fingerprint (sha1 of match node id + stack) and persist mapping in a short-lived store (ttl ~ 24h). header -> fingerprint. Support uses the mapping to show a readable trace.
Liya Chen: That mapping store is basically a cache. We need lifecycle rules and size limits. Also: what about private customer deployments? mapping must be tenant-scoped and optionally disabled.
Sasha Ortiz: Ops concern: storing millions of mappings at peak could be heavy. Maybe only persist when request has debug flag or when decision changed from baseline (i.e., unexpected fallback).
Maya Patel: Product wants default visibility for enterprise plans. Could gate by tenant tier + feature flag.
Jon Reynolds: Now the other item: budget-aware preemption. A few customers want the router to enforce per-route token budgets and preempt/redirect to cheaper models when budgets near exhaustion.
Liya Chen: Two main options: 1) soft score penalty that gradually increases as budget nears zero, 2) hard preempt once threshold hit. Soft is smoother but harder to reason about.
Maya Patel: We should prototype soft first (score delta function), then allow per-tenant threshold for hard cutover. Keep determinism: tie-breaker must be stable. Use hash(tenant_id || request_id) as final tie-breaker so behavior reproducible.
Jon Reynolds: Policy DSL snippet idea (very rough):
```
route {
  when budget_pct < 10% then add_penalty 2000 with ttl 10s
  when budget_pct < 5% then redirect to model:llama-cheap v2
}
```
Liya Chen: Nice. Note: numeric penalties must be normalized across other signals (latency, region). We'll need a global penalty scale doc and a runtime clamp.
Sasha Ortiz: Telemetry: emit decisions as traces with fields {fingerprint, applied_penalties, budget_pct, chosen_model, reason_codes}. Keep size small.
EngInfraBot: Deploy bot: rolling canary for policy-service with explainability store will go to infra-canary in 2h.
Maya Patel: Action items: (1) Jon to draft header + mapping spec + TTL and tenant gating, (2) Liya to design penalty normalization doc and tie-breaker hashing, (3) Sasha to estimate cost of mapping store at 10k TPS and options (redis vs lru local).
Jon Reynolds: I'll drop a short RFC PR by EOD, include sample DSL and telemetry fields.
Liya Chen: FYI — we should consider privacy for PII in expanded traces. Mask tenant request metadata by default.
Sasha Ortiz: +1. Also include an ops switch to disable persistence entirely for private deployments.
Maya Patel: Perfect. If no objections, we'll run canary next week after Jon's RFC. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule postmortem channel synced if canary hits >1% error delta.
Maya Patel: Thanks — closing loop here.
